- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to capture mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a 2–4 day lag correction to align with sentiment reversal.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates long-term upward trends; add 0.5–1.5% per week to forecast if sentiment remains positive.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and history shows volatility, model tends to smooth too much; increase forecast variance by 0.5–1.0% to reflect sentiment uncertainty.
